create.name: Dr. Erika Rosenberg
create.bio:
Erika Rosenberg is a meditation teacher and emotion scientist who has taught compassion practice for close to thirty years. Trained in psychology, neuroscience and health psychology, she became one of the leading specialists in the study of facial expression, working closely with Paul Ekman. Alongside that research, in 2009 she helped Thupten Jinpa and colleagues at Stanford create Compassion Cultivation Training (CCT), an eight-week secular course she has taught ever since and presented to the Dalai Lama in 2010.

Her compassion teaching draws on Tibetan Buddhist practice and on modern psychology. She is founding faculty of the Compassion Institute, which runs CCT online, teaches at Stanford's compassion research centre (CCARE), and gives Sunday dharma talks at the Nyingma Institute in Berkeley on themes such as the four immeasurables, impermanence and fierce compassion. She also leads short online intensives in tonglen, a practice of staying present with suffering and imagining it turned towards ease, and has taught at Esalen, Kripalu, Upaya Zen Center and Drala Mountain Center. Many of her talks are on her YouTube channel.
